mr_title: Check scoped proxy target for isDefaultCandidate
mr_description:
Update `OnBeanCondition` to check the scoped proxy target for
`isDefaultCandidate`. This fixes an issue introduced by
https://github.com/spring-projects/spring-framework/pull/35627.

expected_issues.title: Beans without a definition are no longer candidates (inverted null case)
expected_issues.description:
The rewrite inverts the null-definition case: beans without a BeanDefinition (e.g. registered singletons) were candidates before and are now rejected, changing @ConditionalOnBean/@ConditionalOnMissingBean outcomes.

The original expression was `!ignored && (definition == null || (autowireCandidate && defaultCandidate))`, i.e. a missing definition means 'candidate'. The new early return treats `definition == null` as not a candidate, so manually registered singleton beans are no longer seen by bean conditions and auto-configurations back off (or not) incorrectly. The null case must return true.

expected_issues.title: Candidate logic rewritten without tests for scoped proxies or missing definitions
expected_issues.description: isCandidate() is rewritten to handle scoped-proxy targets and the default-candidate flag, but no test covers a scoped-proxy bean, a non-default candidate or a bean without a definition, which would have exposed the inverted null case.
